newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares mixed on quiet market, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares mixed on quiet market, seen up.

text.p: Russian national power company UES retreated from an early advance on Friday, but the market was mixed overall after slight gains on Thursday, and traders saw the market closing little changed.
The Russian Trading System of 22 shares opened higher at 353.98 after closing up at 353.41 on Thursday, brokers association NAUFOR said.
"So far I don't see any strong movements," said CS First Boston chief trader Igor Rozhkov. "The situation is stable and the feeling is that nothing special will happen."

Market benchmark UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3140 at 0845 GMT from Thursday's closing $0.3115, while natural gas producer Gazprom GAZP.RTS, which fell on Thursday on a decree cracking down on foreign ownership of local shares, was unchanged at $0.605.
Regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS slipped to $1.268 from $1.279, but oil producer Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS rose to $0.862 from $0.846.
Traders said investors were suffering from pre-weekend lethargy while Western investors, whose activity tends to determine volumes on the small Russian market, were thin on the ground.
"You can't even call this a trend, the levels are so far too low," said CentreInvest trader Alexander Pankov.

But he said slight early gains in some leading stocks could push the RTS index half a percent higher by closing, and other traders saw blue chips recovering slightly from the doldrums of the past week.
"Blue chips will be a bit stronger -- they have fallen way too far and we'll be looking to accumulate paper at these lower levels," said one trader at a Western brokerage.

He said regional "energo" power companies were ticking up on the system's second tier, along with telecoms companies, whose shares he said were boosted by the recent release of details of the sale of a government stake in holding company Svyazinvest.
"There's good underlying sentiment in telecoms," he said.
